knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Hands are cleaned prior to patient contact and again after touching anything in the surroundings. Option B names the protective moment; the others misdescribe it.
Washing with water and soap suits grubby hands and situations involving spores or certain viruses. Option B lists those cases; the remaining options do not.
Artificial nails have been linked to heavier organism loads, which is why the guideline discourages them. The other choices lack that support.

practicalCriteria: Learner performs a full alcohol hand rub, showing coverage and drying, and states which moment applies.
Learner washes a simulated soiled hand using soap plus water, dries it, and names a situation where that route is the right choice over a rub.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Hand hygiene self-check entry for one shift
stopWorkCriteria: Soiled hands and no access to soap or running water
Skin is broken and the learner has no waterproof dressing
The learner shows an allergic or irritant reaction to a product
